mentions.description: An idea for a terminal that uses a proportional-width font instead of a monospace font, so characters like "i" and "w" take up their appropriate horizontal space rather than identical width. The author notes table output from commands like ls -l or top would remain aligned by spending cycles doing math, something now practical because computers are fast and no longer need to conserve cycles.
mentions.problem: Terminals use monospace fonts in which every character — including "i" and "w" — occupies the same horizontal space, a legacy of slow computers when cycles and bits had to be counted, wasting space and making text less readable.
mentions.author: solyin
